problem: The noise gain is quoted as 1 + R_f/R₁ and trap 5 applies it to 'the summer'. That value is the noise gain of the four-resistor subtractor (or of a single-input inverting amplifier). In an n-input inverting summer the offset voltage sees all input resistors in parallel to ground, so its gain is 1 + R_f/(R₁∥R₂∥…∥Rₙ), which is much larger. Example: with R_f = 10 kΩ and three 10 kΩ inputs the offset gain is 1 + 10k/3.33k = 4, not 2. A student will under-estimate the output offset of the summer.
fix: Write: 'In the subtractor the op-amp offset voltage appears at the output multiplied by the noise gain 1 + R_f/R₁. In an n-input inverting summer the same offset is multiplied by 1 + R_f/R_eq, where R_eq = R₁∥R₂∥…∥Rₙ, so keep R_f no larger than needed. Neither gain is the signal gain.' In trap 5, replace 'the noise gain 1 + R_f/R₁, not by the signal gain of the summer' with 'the noise gain of the circuit (1 + R_f/R₁ for the subtractor, 1 + R_f/R_eq for the summer), not by its signal gain'.
